title.en: Goals one step at a time

text.en: How long can you hold naukasana? 20 seconds? Setting a small goal and achieving it is the key to success.

The key to success is to set and achieve goals. Examples: holding naukasana for 20 seconds, T-balance on one leg for 20 seconds or jumping jacks for 60 seconds.
Every individual sets different goals based on their needs. Some goals we should all try to achieve, like keeping our balance and growing strong.
Crab wheel: sit crouching with legs a little wider than the shoulders, tuck the elbows in, and on the whistle move hands and feet sideways one by one and roll over. It builds upper body strength and flexibility.
Listen Carefully: jog towards the finish line, and when the teacher calls a movement, such as walking on toes, heels, hopping or side shuffle, do it. It develops response time.
Did you know? Your brain gets the signal, makes a decision and tells your body what to do in less than a second.

problem.en: How can you set a small goal for balance?

text.en: Choose a pose like T-balance on one leg.

why.en: Start with something you can do.

prompt.en: Why do we set goals in exercise?

points.en: Set small goals such as holding a pose for 20 seconds.
Crab wheel builds strength and flexibility.
